summary: The Westminster Confession, which the Presbyterian Church in America holds as a doctrinal standard, teaches that at death the souls of the righteous are made perfect in holiness and received into the highest heavens to await the redemption of their bodies, while the souls of the wicked are cast into hell. At the last day all the dead will be raised with the selfsame bodies, and Christ will judge all. The purpose of the judgment is to manifest the glory of God's mercy in the salvation of the elect and of his justice in the damnation of the reprobate; the righteous go into everlasting life and the wicked are cast into everlasting punishment.

points.question: Is there a purification after death?
points.answer: At death the souls of the righteous, made perfect in holiness, go to the highest heavens; the souls of the wicked are cast into hell. The Confession names no third place.

points.question: What is the final state of the wicked?
points.answer: The judgment manifests God's justice in the damnation of the reprobate, who are cast into everlasting punishment.

points.question: What happens when Christ returns?
points.answer: At the last day the dead are raised with the selfsame bodies and all are judged; the elect enter everlasting life.

rights.note: The Confession's wording dates from 1646. The edition read is a modern-spelling web copy; its rights are not separately confirmed, so only one sentence is quoted.

review.note: Chapter 32 (sections 1-2) and chapter 33 (section 2) read in one web copy (the-highway.com) on 2026-11-12; the end of 32.1, which says the Scripture acknowledges no other place for separated souls, and chapter 33's opening were not read. "No purgatory" is our reading of 32.1 for that reason. The PCA's own copy was not compared. Not yet checked by a second reviewer.
